[CONTRIBUTE OTHER >>](https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/major-fec-deadline/?utm_campaign=20250331&utm_medium=email&utm_source=TLC_A/&amount=other)

I’ve been by Dan’s side through 5 deployments as a Navy SEAL, through his devastating injury in Afghanistan, and now as he serves in the U.S. House of Representatives.

And through it all, I can tell you that Dan is more committed than ever to fight for our shared American values.

He’s dedicated to work alongside President Trump and leaders in the House and Senate to deliver on the promise that is America.

Dan has been fighting for you and me, and all Americans, for his entire adult life – first on the battlefield, and now in the halls of Congress.

I know Dan best and can tell you that Dan is truly one of a kind. He is a husband, a father, a soldier, and a champion for America in Congress.

And he needs us now.

[CONTRIBUTE NOW>>](https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/major-fec-deadline/?utm_campaign=20250331&utm_medium=email&utm_source=TLC_A)

The next 2 years are going to be different from what we’ve seen in the past. Dan is already encountering more attacks than we’ve ever seen and its only March.

Unfortunately, these campaigns seem to get longer and longer, and they definitely get more and more expensive.

This is why it is so important that we come to Dan’s aid now – so that he can reload his campaign warchest and not fall behind as the first quarter comes to an end.

Whether it is gearing up from well-funded challengers or just having the resources to fight back against lies and deceit from the Left, Dan needs our help.

He has always been there for us, and I know that you have been there for him in the past as well, but I’m hoping Dan can also count on you now.

[Please make a contribution to Dan’s campaign to ensure that he is able to replenish his warchest and have the resources necessary to fight off attacks from the Left in his continued service to America in Congress.](https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/major-fec-deadline/?utm_campaign=20250331&utm_medium=email&utm_source=TLC_A)

Thank you,

Tara Crenshaw

### BLUE LETTER: Trump Flirts with Dictatorship--Because Two Terms Aren't Enough for the Narcissistic Rug-Rat
Donald Trump's latest "joke" about a third term--where he coyly suggests a puppet-VP like JD Vance could warm the seat before handing it back to Dear Leader--isn't comedy; it's the autocratic equivalent of drunk-texting the Constitution at 3 a.m. (which Pete Hegseth should get to any day now).
This isn't satire. But a test balloon floated by a greasy, gauche, despot who sees Putin as a model. What dolt Don's suggesting is what Mother Russia's man-boobed, tyrant _did there_. The Constitution from the end of the Soviet Union only allowed two terms, so it was President Putin from 2000-2008. He put plaything, Dmitri Medvedev, in the role from 2008-2012. Then he changed the rules and returned. **Forever.**
Trump treats our 22nd Amendment like a Groupon code--annoying, but to be ignored if you whine loud enough. And sure, the Founders warned us about _this exact scenario_ , but who has time for 18th-century buzzkill, like law, when you're measuring the Oval Office for a new La-Z-Boy and golden crapper? | | | | | Dear Friend,
This week, we pause to honor someone who played a meaningful and lasting role in the work of Governing Group.
Mia Love was not only a member of our founding board—she was a friend, a mentor, and a trusted voice around the table. Her deep relationships with many of our board members shaped our work in profound ways. She challenged us to lead with clarity, to listen with compassion, and to stay grounded in the purpose of public service.
Mia’s contributions to public life were bold and far-reaching. As the first Black Republican woman elected to Congress, she broke barriers and opened doors for others. Even when her health limited her participation, her presence on our board was a reminder of what principled leadership looks like—and the kind of courage it takes to lead with both strength and grace.
Our deepest condolences go out to Mia’s family and loved ones. We are mourning with you, and honoring her by continuing the work she believed in.
Our board remains committed to building the kind of political leadership Mia exemplified –principled, collaborative, and worthy of the people it serves.
With care,Governing Group

Mia Love was not only a member of our founding board—she was a friend, a mentor, and a trusted voice around the table. Her deep relationships with many of our board members shaped our work in profound ways. She challenged us to lead with clarity, to listen with compassion, and to stay grounded in the purpose of public service. Mia’s contributions to public life were bold and far-reaching. As the first Black Republican woman elected to Congress, she broke barriers and opened doors for others. Our deepest condolences go out to Mia’s family and loved ones. We are mourning with you, and honoring her by continuing the work she believed in. body:
I don’t want us to take our eye off the ball
#
Team — I know you’re probably getting a lot of emails today.
That’s because midnight tonight is the FEC fundraising deadline for campaigns across the country. The first FEC deadline under Trump’s new presidency. It’s a big deal.
But I don’t want us to take our eye off the ball. Because tomorrow in Wisconsin, voters will head to the polls to elect a new state Supreme Court Justice.
This race will have a huge impact, not just on Wisconsin, but on our entire nation. The far-right understands this — that’s why Trump has personally endorsed the ultra-conservative candidate in the race, and why Elon Musk and his allies have spent over $10 million on ads supporting him.
If their candidate wins, we should expect him to follow the new authoritarian Trump playbook.
They could roll back the clock on fair maps and gerrymander more House seats for the GOP.
They could disenfranchise voters en masse from heavily Democratic neighborhoods and backgrounds.
**They could even set themselves up to nullify the results of future elections if they don’t like the outcome.**
On the other hand, if our candidate, Judge Susan Crawford, wins we will cement a pro-choice, pro-worker, pro-democracy majority on the court for the next two years that can continue the progress we’re seeing in Wisconsin right now.
So, with lots of GOTV efforts happening today and tomorrow, and last minute ads still going up on TV and online, I’m asking you one last time:

Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, is one of the biggest spenders in the Wisconsin Supreme Court race — spending more than $19 million (and counting) in support of the conservative candidate. Here’s why, in Musk’s own words:
> _“[This election] will decide how congressional districts are drawn in Wisconsin, which if the other candidate wins, instead of Justice Schimel, then the Democrats will attempt to redraw the districts and cause Wisconsin to lose two Republican seats. In my opinion that’s the most important thing, which is a big deal given that the congressional majority is so razor-thin. It could cause the House to switch to Democrat[ic] if that redrawing takes place.”_

| | | Donald Trump is wrecking our economy, alienating our allies, and putting America on a path to devastation. [**We can't afford to wait until 2029 for his presidency to end. We need to remove him NOW.**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T523740cb-5d31-4a87-b90e-989ea9c6116d/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) If just half of Senate Republicans joined with Democrats, we'd have enough votes to remove him (after impeachment by the House). We need to put pressure on Republicans to do this. They should not get a free pass just because we expect them to be spineless. Plus, the crashing stock market and foreign policy blunders are scaring Congressional Republicans, who face reelection. We need to take advantage of this to separate them from Trump. Yes, Vance would be no picnic, but Trump is the clear and present danger to our nation, and we need to remove him ASAP. **[Add your name, and tell Congress to remove Trump NOW. America can't wait until 2029.](https://default.salsalabs.org/T10412a4a-5e68-4926-8602-c760a2919165/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) **

The GOP’s real plan has been made crystal clear: less taxes for more billionaires.
| | | | | [](https://wb7c9thbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001r0QuG48dD_kVuzGx7h87zHSf4Voo3ialFBdMkW4ovNRgh-YbmrX1fHBW0frsVJinlpqcw1WzKyYSIxkPRURdBda4V4VizkK0MPteL9tH2DVSoMrHV_FG9xiicKpQLFPP2vdM0ENbwKGWc4GcAKPMDz5cJfme0IWJB8ihPH0MkOuHl9rpqJBBQ7JF9XW6OM5cVd4jlg0_eketr-QvdDc1-B96IpEuJHUx6GSxgIqrcyY=&c=dX5X-mNUN4AoMBw9bsDGhOZLzig1X51Zw8ys77VwrhjDzEzHzYNpiQ==&ch=Uq8pMb0W5SQA5rtjs8-3zHtqjWgMAblThBiolR7odn-06pOR0YvoQQ==)
---
Team,
It is the night before our Election Day, and things are less chaotic at Weil HQ than you would think. Here's why:
We are organized and feeling confident heading into Election Day. Your support has fueled an unprecedented GOTV operation that is mobilizing thousands of volunteers from all across the country to fight hard and compete in a red district that Trump won by over 30 points last year. It is nothing short of incredible.
How is this possible? Two reasons:
First, hundreds of thousands of donors pulled together to support our campaign from the very beginning. YOU have made this a race, and I want to extend my deepest thanks for all that you have done to get us to this point, Friend.
Second, since Trump returned to power, the GOP's real plan has been made crystal clear: less taxes for more billionaires. Working people in districts like mine know when they are getting screwed. My constituents, both Republican and Democrat, do not support tax cuts for the wealthy or government-backed scams that further enrich those who already have power and wealth.
That's why this election could be the beginning of the end for MAGA. But things are far from over -- we have to work twice as hard in these final hours.
---
| | | | My Friend--We are the resistance to Trump's MAGA fascism. We are the frontline, right here and right now.
With so much on the line, every moment, every dollar, and every door knocked could make the difference. Dear Fellow American,

I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter.

It will only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our nation's future.

A movement is growing, led by progressives—but supported by many well-meaning Americans—to change the way we elect our president. In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution.

That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on Presidential Selection.

By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue—views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using the link below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=17x64w94u6dko905zho30spxfw4lkgq6k7ifi7jfhj6ng73fwkejuye4fyitet44bg5v1wszcbl6ifpbjn7on255nty28bh7q3ybtynubf77sxb58hbig2y0bf8ytk9v7rybbw8cnmyp805awr6ka3lcvvuu5i&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=su07ck&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=su07ck&__onlt=t

Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?

YES
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=su07ck&__onlt=t

NO
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=su07ck&__onlt=t

For most of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it was considered essential to preserving free and representative government.

But today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with a proper grounding in American civics—too many Americans simply don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states.

These efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including American civics) to thousands of American educators and homeschoolers.

Your answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty—including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this is especially important in this critical time for America's future.

So please share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

You can take the survey using this secure link I've provided below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=17x64w94u6dko905zho30spxfw4lkgq6k86ska5xfdk91yelkxlm4tyrvwybrzma6oo259j95dh3l5q9p6m05pt91or7oxtfzgnymx8t0f3knsvz9u2ohwikr0mvxwiufbnyltbvggkyjok57r20pftrygs6xe&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=su07ck&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=su07ck&__onlt=t

And after you take your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Since 1844, Hillsdale has been "pursuing truth and defending liberty." Today, it does so through its extensive educational outreach efforts while refusing to accept ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of federal or state student grants or loans.

The support of private citizens like you is essential to our work.

Please represent your state and take the National Survey on Presidential Selection today. Thank you for your time and attention—and for your friendship and support of liberty.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn

President, Hillsdale College

Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

subject: RITE Asks Court to Restore Voter Registration Identify Verification in Pennsylvania
body:
Asks court to strike down state directive to ignore discrepancies in voter ID information |
---
| |
---
| |
# **RITE Asks Court to Restore Voter Registration Identify Verification in Pennsylvania **

(Harrisburg, Pennsylvania – March 31, 2025) - Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (“RITE”), a non-profit organization that supports litigation to protect election security and integrity, today [filed a motion](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=2fd211efbe&e=ea91f782ea) for summary judgment in its case seeking to restore common sense to how Pennsylvania verifies the identity of those registering to vote. RITE requested Pennsylvania’s Commonwealth Court strike down a 2018 Department of State directive which purports to force county election officials to register individuals even when they provide identifying information on their applications that does not match corresponding information found in official government databases.

That directive, which instructed local officials to ignore discrepancies in information such as driver’s license numbers or Social Security numbers, contradicts state law, which requires that information provided on registration applications be complete and consistent. It also amounts to an unlawful rulemaking.

“Pennsylvania law requires county commissioners ... to review new voter registration applications for completeness and consistency before accepting them,” read the original suit, which was filed on behalf of a member of the Potter County Board of Elections on November 4, 2024. “This, in turn, requires commissioners to use accessible databases to evaluate whether the driver’s license numbers or the last four digits of social security numbers supplied on the application match the name of the applicant.”

Even with this requirement in state law, the Department of State twice erroneously informed county commissioners – once in 2006 and again in 2018 – that the law demanded the opposite, and ordered elections officials to register individuals even when their identifying information did not match.

“It’s madness to ask officials to crosscheck an individual’s identifying information on voter registration forms with official databases and when that information doesn’t match demand local officials accept the registration,” said RITE Spokesman Tim Murtaugh. “Inaccurate voter registrations are at the root of many of our election integrity and administration problems and they need to be fixed. RITE’s suit seeks to restore sanity and integrity to Pennsylvania’s registration system and we are confident the court will agree that the Department of State’s directive is unlawful.”

RITE is seeking immediate court intervention to strike down the directive, restore election officials’ ability to verify voters’ identity, and prevent fraudulent or duplicate registrations from undermining election integrity.

Look: I get that this isn’t popular for the bureaucrats, the deep state, and the career politicians like my opponents.
Look: I get that this isn't popular for the bureaucrats, the deep state, and the career politicians like my opponents.

| | | | [](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews._-1EieSGgIn0g)
---
Hello.

Nothing grinds my gears more than unelected, holier-than-thou bureaucrats in Washington DC - and in state capitals across the country - who spend your money like drunken sailors with nothing to show for it.

I campaigned for President Trump so he'd take a BLOWTORCH to the federal managerial class... **And now I 'm running for Ohio Governor to obliterate the business-as-usual waste at the state level, too.**

Whether you live here or not, you deserve a government that works for you. And at the heart of this campaign, I'm running to return power to your hands - and keep more money in your pocket.
| ❌ We will gut the managerial bureaucracy and eliminate waste
---
❌ We will eliminate the state income tax
❌ We will put Ohio on track to eliminate property taxes

_This is your money - NOT the government's._

Look: I get that this isn't popular for the bureaucrats, the Deep State, and the career politicians like my opponents.

That's why they're trashing my name in the press and trying to destroy the only Trump-endorsed MAGA conservative in this race. Luckily, I have a hunch folks like you prefer paying no state income tax, saving on property taxes, and eliminating waste in our government.

**[Now that I've launched my candidacy for Governor, will you join my campaign today?](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.-mhWeh0Zkhk3Dg "Now that I’ve launched my candidacy for Governor, will you join my campaign today?")** **I 'm staring down my FIRST end-of-quarter fundraising deadline since launch, and I'm still about 5,500 donations short of my goal.**

I'm not running to rub elbows with party bosses or special interests. I'm running to transform my home state into a low-tax, business-friendly heaven in the heartland of America.

We should be a state that celebrates hard work, not rejects it. And we will set an example for the rest of the country.

_So - in the final days before my deadline - I'm personally asking for your support:_

body:
Hi friend,
I know what you’re thinking... **_“Another fundraising email... really, Kristen?”_**
Look, I get it. I know, especially around this time of the month, your inbox is full of emails from other campaigns and organizations.
But the truth is, emails like this are one of our best tools to keep our campaign moving forward. And with national Republicans already targeting me, it’s so important to build grassroots support that can’t be bought or drowned out by outside money.
Winning this race wasn’t easy in 2024, and with Republicans looking to expand their majority, keeping this seat next year will be an even bigger challenge.

"**3 dead, more than 200 rescued in South Texas after severe storms cause flooding** ," AP's **Valerie Gonzalez** and Texas Tribune's**Berenice Garcia** -- "Drenching rain along the Texas-Mexico border let up Friday, but rescues were still ongoing a day after severe storms trapped residents in their homes, forced drivers to abandon their vehicles on flooded roads and shut down an airport.

Local officials also reported at least three people died from the rainstorm.

Hidalgo County officials said there was no immediate information on the three deaths, only that they involved law enforcement. U.S. Customs and Border Protection reported one death involving U.S. Border Patrol agents. Agents approached a vehicle suspected of being involved in human smuggling that was stopped at a flooded road in Edcouch. As the agents approached, the driver attempted to cross the flooded street, plunging the vehicle into a canal.

In Harlingen, officials said their city received a record-breaking 21.5**** inches of rain this week, beating its all-time two-day total rainfall record set in 1912. The heaviest rainfall arrived on Thursday causing severe flooding that had authorities rescuing more than 200 residents, with another 200 people still waiting to be rescued.

"This of course has been a historic and challenging event for the city. But Harlingen is strong. We have faced adversity before and we will get through this together," Mayor **Norma Sepulveda** said at a Friday afternoon news conference.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/53e8632d-046a-476e-b266-b515120f4113?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In Alamo, the police and fire department responded to more than 100 water rescues, including people stranded in their vehicles and trapped in their homes, Fire Department Chief **R.C. Flores** said at a news conference Friday afternoon.

Officials estimated a couple hundred homes in Alamo were flooded by the heavy rainfall.

Flores said Alamo was one of many cities in the Rio Grande Valley in South Texas that were flooded and had damage from Thursday's thunderstorms but that all were working to help their residents.

"I assure the public that we are assessing the situation on the hour, every hour. We're constantly going out, not just in our city," Flores said. "Just because the storm is over, it doesn't mean that the emergencies and the disaster is over. We are going to continue to work as long as we need to."

Weslaco Mayor **Adrian Gonzalez** said his city was inundated with about 14 inches of rain, prompting 30 to 40 water rescues of stranded motorists and residents trapped in their homes by rising floodwaters.

"It's a historic rainstorm and it's affecting all the Valley, not just Weslaco. It's just so much water in a short period of time," Gonzalez told reporters at a news conference.

Television news footage from flooded communities in South Texas showed multiple waterlogged cars abandoned on streets on Thursday and drivers waiting on sidewalks for the floodwaters to recede.

Between 6 inches and 12 inches of rain fell in many parts of South Texas in the past 24 hours, according to the National Weather Service. In neighboring Cameron County, officials asked Gov.**Greg Abbott** to declare a disaster for the county after more than 17 inches of rain caused significant flooding.

"The rainfall amounts we received have been record-setting, and not in a good way. All county resources are being utilized right now, and we are assisting in all ways possible," Cameron County Judge **Eddie Trevi ño Jr.**, the county's top elected official, said in a Facebook post.

Valley International Airport in Harlingen was closed on Friday and all flights were canceled due to area flooding.
"We are working tirelessly to reopen and focused on ensuring safety," airport officials said in a statement." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/b45b6e5c-94fd-4a61-9940-56f740e648ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

TOP NEWS "3 dead, more than 200 rescued in South Texas after severe storms cause flooding ," AP's Valerie Gonzalez and Texas Tribune'sBerenice Garcia -- "Drenching rain along the Texas-Mexico border let up Friday, but rescues were still ongoing a day after severe storms trapped residents in their homes, forced drivers to abandon their vehicles on flooded roads and shut down an airport. Local officials also reported at least three people died from the rainstorm. Hidalgo County officials said there was no immediate information on the three deaths, only that they involved law enforcement. U.S. Customs and Border Protection reported one death involving U.S. Border Patrol agents. Agents approached a vehicle suspected of being involved in human smuggling that was stopped at a flooded road in Edcouch. As the agents approached, the driver attempted to cross the flooded street, plunging the vehicle into a canal. In Harlingen, officials said their city received a record-breaking 21.5** inches of rain this week, beating its all-time two-day total rainfall record set in 1912. The heaviest rainfall arrived on Thursday causing severe flooding that had authorities rescuing more than 200 residents, with another 200 people still waiting to be rescued. "This of course has been a historic and challenging event for the city. But Harlingen is strong. We have faced adversity before and we will get through this together," Mayor Norma Sepulveda said at a Friday afternoon news conference. In Alamo, the police and fire department responded to more than 100 water rescues, including people stranded in their vehicles and trapped in their homes, Fire Department Chief R.C. Flores said at a news conference Friday afternoon. Officials estimated a couple hundred homes in Alamo were flooded by the heavy rainfall. Flores said Alamo was one of many cities in the Rio Grande Valley in South Texas that were flooded and had damage from Thursday's thunderstorms but that all were working to help their residents. "I assure the public that we are assessing the situation on the hour, every hour. We're constantly going out, not just in our city," Flores said. "Just because the storm is over, it doesn't mean that the emergencies and the disaster is over. We are going to continue to work as long as we need to." Weslaco Mayor Adrian Gonzalez said his city was inundated with about 14 inches of rain, prompting 30 to 40 water rescues of stranded motorists and residents trapped in their homes by rising floodwaters. "It's a historic rainstorm and it's affecting all the Valley, not just Weslaco. It's just so much water in a short period of time," Gonzalez told reporters at a news conference. Television news footage from flooded communities in South Texas showed multiple waterlogged cars abandoned on streets on Thursday and drivers waiting on sidewalks for the floodwaters to recede. Between 6 inches and 12 inches of rain fell in many parts of South Texas in the past 24 hours, according to the National Weather Service. In neighboring Cameron County, officials asked Gov.Greg Abbott to declare a disaster for the county after more than 17 inches of rain caused significant flooding. "The rainfall amounts we received have been record-setting, and not in a good way. All county resources are being utilized right now, and we are assisting in all ways possible," Cameron County Judge Eddie Trevi ño Jr., the county's top elected official, said in a Facebook post. Valley International Airport in Harlingen was closed on Friday and all flights were canceled due to area flooding. "We are working tirelessly to reopen and focused on ensuring safety," airport officials said in a statement." "**3 dead, more than 200 rescued in South Texas after severe storms cause flooding** ," AP's **Valerie Gonzalez** and Texas Tribune's**Berenice Garcia** -- "Drenching rain along the Texas-Mexico border let up Friday, but rescues were still ongoing a day after severe storms trapped residents in their homes, forced drivers to abandon their vehicles on flooded roads and shut down an airport.

Local officials also reported at least three people died from the rainstorm.

Hidalgo County officials said there was no immediate information on the three deaths, only that they involved law enforcement. U.S. Customs and Border Protection reported one death involving U.S. Border Patrol agents. Agents approached a vehicle suspected of being involved in human smuggling that was stopped at a flooded road in Edcouch. As the agents approached, the driver attempted to cross the flooded street, plunging the vehicle into a canal.

In Harlingen, officials said their city received a record-breaking 21.5**** inches of rain this week, beating its all-time two-day total rainfall record set in 1912. The heaviest rainfall arrived on Thursday causing severe flooding that had authorities rescuing more than 200 residents, with another 200 people still waiting to be rescued.

"This of course has been a historic and challenging event for the city. But Harlingen is strong. We have faced adversity before and we will get through this together," Mayor **Norma Sepulveda** said at a Friday afternoon news conference.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/0fef345a-27cc-4ee8-9339-9213360722fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In Alamo, the police and fire department responded to more than 100 water rescues, including people stranded in their vehicles and trapped in their homes, Fire Department Chief **R.C. Flores** said at a news conference Friday afternoon.

Officials estimated a couple hundred homes in Alamo were flooded by the heavy rainfall.

Flores said Alamo was one of many cities in the Rio Grande Valley in South Texas that were flooded and had damage from Thursday's thunderstorms but that all were working to help their residents.

"I assure the public that we are assessing the situation on the hour, every hour. We're constantly going out, not just in our city," Flores said. "Just because the storm is over, it doesn't mean that the emergencies and the disaster is over. We are going to continue to work as long as we need to."

Weslaco Mayor **Adrian Gonzalez** said his city was inundated with about 14 inches of rain, prompting 30 to 40 water rescues of stranded motorists and residents trapped in their homes by rising floodwaters.

"It's a historic rainstorm and it's affecting all the Valley, not just Weslaco. It's just so much water in a short period of time," Gonzalez told reporters at a news conference.

Television news footage from flooded communities in South Texas showed multiple waterlogged cars abandoned on streets on Thursday and drivers waiting on sidewalks for the floodwaters to recede.

Between 6 inches and 12 inches of rain fell in many parts of South Texas in the past 24 hours, according to the National Weather Service. In neighboring Cameron County, officials asked Gov.**Greg Abbott** to declare a disaster for the county after more than 17 inches of rain caused significant flooding.

"The rainfall amounts we received have been record-setting, and not in a good way. All county resources are being utilized right now, and we are assisting in all ways possible," Cameron County Judge **Eddie Trevi ño Jr.**, the county's top elected official, said in a Facebook post.

Valley International Airport in Harlingen was closed on Friday and all flights were canceled due to area flooding.
"We are working tirelessly to reopen and focused on ensuring safety," airport officials said in a statement." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/31a7e6f8-a289-4d97-8365-2e932a8b380c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

TOP NEWS "3 dead, more than 200 rescued in South Texas after severe storms cause flooding ," AP's Valerie Gonzalez and Texas Tribune'sBerenice Garcia -- "Drenching rain along the Texas-Mexico border let up Friday, but rescues were still ongoing a day after severe storms trapped residents in their homes, forced drivers to abandon their vehicles on flooded roads and shut down an airport. Local officials also reported at least three people died from the rainstorm. Hidalgo County officials said there was no immediate information on the three deaths, only that they involved law enforcement. U.S. Customs and Border Protection reported one death involving U.S. Border Patrol agents. Agents approached a vehicle suspected of being involved in human smuggling that was stopped at a flooded road in Edcouch. As the agents approached, the driver attempted to cross the flooded street, plunging the vehicle into a canal. In Harlingen, officials said their city received a record-breaking 21.5** inches of rain this week, beating its all-time two-day total rainfall record set in 1912. The heaviest rainfall arrived on Thursday causing severe flooding that had authorities rescuing more than 200 residents, with another 200 people still waiting to be rescued. "This of course has been a historic and challenging event for the city. But Harlingen is strong. We have faced adversity before and we will get through this together," Mayor Norma Sepulveda said at a Friday afternoon news conference. In Alamo, the police and fire department responded to more than 100 water rescues, including people stranded in their vehicles and trapped in their homes, Fire Department Chief R.C. Flores said at a news conference Friday afternoon. Officials estimated a couple hundred homes in Alamo were flooded by the heavy rainfall. Flores said Alamo was one of many cities in the Rio Grande Valley in South Texas that were flooded and had damage from Thursday's thunderstorms but that all were working to help their residents. "I assure the public that we are assessing the situation on the hour, every hour. We're constantly going out, not just in our city," Flores said. "Just because the storm is over, it doesn't mean that the emergencies and the disaster is over. We are going to continue to work as long as we need to." Weslaco Mayor Adrian Gonzalez said his city was inundated with about 14 inches of rain, prompting 30 to 40 water rescues of stranded motorists and residents trapped in their homes by rising floodwaters. "It's a historic rainstorm and it's affecting all the Valley, not just Weslaco. It's just so much water in a short period of time," Gonzalez told reporters at a news conference. Television news footage from flooded communities in South Texas showed multiple waterlogged cars abandoned on streets on Thursday and drivers waiting on sidewalks for the floodwaters to recede. Between 6 inches and 12 inches of rain fell in many parts of South Texas in the past 24 hours, according to the National Weather Service. In neighboring Cameron County, officials asked Gov.Greg Abbott to declare a disaster for the county after more than 17 inches of rain caused significant flooding. "The rainfall amounts we received have been record-setting, and not in a good way. All county resources are being utilized right now, and we are assisting in all ways possible," Cameron County Judge Eddie Trevi ño Jr., the county's top elected official, said in a Facebook post. Valley International Airport in Harlingen was closed on Friday and all flights were canceled due to area flooding. "We are working tirelessly to reopen and focused on ensuring safety," airport officials said in a statement." “**3 dead, more than 200 rescued in South Texas after severe storms cause flooding** ,” AP's **Valerie Gonzalez** and Texas Tribune's**Berenice Garcia** — “Drenching rain along the Texas-Mexico border let up Friday, but rescues were still ongoing a day after severe storms trapped residents in their homes, forced drivers to abandon their vehicles on flooded roads and shut down an airport.

Local officials also reported at least three people died from the rainstorm.

Hidalgo County officials said there was no immediate information on the three deaths, only that they involved law enforcement. U.S. Customs and Border Protection reported one death involving U.S. Border Patrol agents. Agents approached a vehicle suspected of being involved in human smuggling that was stopped at a flooded road in Edcouch. As the agents approached, the driver attempted to cross the flooded street, plunging the vehicle into a canal.

Flores said Alamo was one of many cities in the Rio Grande Valley in South Texas that were flooded and had damage from Thursday's thunderstorms but that all were working to help their residents.

"I assure the public that we are assessing the situation on the hour, every hour. We're constantly going out, not just in our city," Flores said. "Just because the storm is over, it doesn't mean that the emergencies and the disaster is over. We are going to continue to work as long as we need to."

Weslaco Mayor **Adrian Gonzalez** said his city was inundated with about 14 inches of rain, prompting 30 to 40 water rescues of stranded motorists and residents trapped in their homes by rising floodwaters.

"It's a historic rainstorm and it's affecting all the Valley, not just Weslaco. It's just so much water in a short period of time," Gonzalez told reporters at a news conference.

Television news footage from flooded communities in South Texas showed multiple waterlogged cars abandoned on streets on Thursday and drivers waiting on sidewalks for the floodwaters to recede.

Between 6 inches and 12 inches of rain fell in many parts of South Texas in the past 24 hours, according to the National Weather Service. In neighboring Cameron County, officials asked Gov.**Greg Abbott** to declare a disaster for the county after more than 17 inches of rain caused significant flooding.

"The rainfall amounts we received have been record-setting, and not in a good way. All county resources are being utilized right now, and we are assisting in all ways possible," Cameron County Judge **Eddie Treviño Jr.** , the county's top elected official, said in a Facebook post.

Valley International Airport in Harlingen was closed on Friday and all flights were canceled due to area flooding.
"We are working tirelessly to reopen and focused on ensuring safety," airport officials said in a statement." Local officials also reported at least three people died from the rainstorm. Hidalgo County officials said there was no immediate information on the three deaths, only that they involved law enforcement. U.S. Customs and Border Protection reported one death involving U.S. Border Patrol agents. Agents approached a vehicle suspected of being involved in human smuggling that was stopped at a flooded road in Edcouch. As the agents approached, the driver attempted to cross the flooded street, plunging the vehicle into a canal. » In Harlingen, officials said their city received a record-breaking 21.5 inches of rain this week, beating its all-time two-day total rainfall record set in 1912. The heaviest rainfall arrived on Thursday causing severe flooding that had authorities rescuing more than 200 residents, with another 200 people still waiting to be rescued. "This of course has been a historic and challenging event for the city. But Harlingen is strong. We have faced adversity before and we will get through this together," Mayor Norma Sepulveda said at a Friday afternoon news conference. » In Alamo, the police and fire department responded to more than 100 water rescues, including people stranded in their vehicles and trapped in their homes, Fire Department Chief R.C. Flores said at a news conference Friday afternoon. Officials estimated a couple hundred homes in Alamo were flooded by the heavy rainfall. Flores said Alamo was one of many cities in the Rio Grande Valley in South Texas that were flooded and had damage from Thursday's thunderstorms but that all were working to help their residents. "I assure the public that we are assessing the situation on the hour, every hour. We're constantly going out, not just in our city," Flores said. "Just because the storm is over, it doesn't mean that the emergencies and the disaster is over. We are going to continue to work as long as we need to." Weslaco Mayor Adrian Gonzalez said his city was inundated with about 14 inches of rain, prompting 30 to 40 water rescues of stranded motorists and residents trapped in their homes by rising floodwaters. "It's a historic rainstorm and it's affecting all the Valley, not just Weslaco. It's just so much water in a short period of time," Gonzalez told reporters at a news conference. Television news footage from flooded communities in South Texas showed multiple waterlogged cars abandoned on streets on Thursday and drivers waiting on sidewalks for the floodwaters to recede. Between 6 inches and 12 inches of rain fell in many parts of South Texas in the past 24 hours, according to the National Weather Service. In neighboring Cameron County, officials asked Gov.Greg Abbott to declare a disaster for the county after more than 17 inches of rain caused significant flooding. "The rainfall amounts we received have been record-setting, and not in a good way. All county resources are being utilized right now, and we are assisting in all ways possible," Cameron County Judge Eddie Treviño Jr. , the county's top elected official, said in a Facebook post. Valley International Airport in Harlingen was closed on Friday and all flights were canceled due to area flooding. body:
I didn’t take the usual path to Congress.
| [ ](https://takano4ca.us/l/esBRR7ZXqh2a?t=xZ00fpRhr7zH)
---
**I didn’t take the usual path to Congress, Peter.** I wasn’t handpicked by party insiders, shaped by Washington consultants, or carefully designed based on the latest polling. No, my commitment to public service was _built over generations_ —rooted in resilience, perseverance, and an unshakable belief in a better future.

**My parents and grandparents didn’t have that same choice.** During World War II, they were sent to Japanese American internment camps, stripped of their rights, and forced to rebuild from nothing—all because of racist, fear-driven policies. [](https://takano4ca.us/l/90xbb10bWziF) **Even after being treated as second-class citizens** , they never gave up on this country. They taught me that loving America means fighting to **_make it_** live up to its promise.

That lesson shaped my entire life. It’s why I spent 20 years as a public school teacher. It’s why I ran for Congress—despite the bigotry I faced when my Republican opponent forcibly outed me in 1994. And it’s why I’m still fighting today.

Because now, we’re facing a new wave of extremism. The MAGA Majority in the House isn’t just attacking immigrants, LGBTQ+ Americans, and women’s rights—they’re openly scheming to cut Social Security, the lifeline millions of seniors rely on. They want to dismantle decades of progress, and if we don’t stop them, they just might succeed. [**We cannot let that happen. The only way to stop MAGA’s dangerous agenda is to narrow their majority in the House and flip key seats. If we sit on the sidelines, they win. But if we fight together, we can stop them. So I’m counting on you – will you chip in $7 today to help elect Democrats and protect our future? »**](https://takano4ca.us/l/yHxOvgFFDR2I) | [CHIP IN $7 TO FLIP THE MAGA MAJORITY! »](https://takano4ca.us/l/YOBBNbeaTLzH)

Elon Musk has spent the last month (and tens of millions of dollars) trying to buy himself a shiny new Supreme Court seat in Wisconsin. | | | Peter, Elon Musk has spent the last month (and tens of millions of dollars) trying to buy himself a shiny new Supreme Court seat in Wisconsin. How we spend the next 24 hours will decide whether or not it worked. We have one more day to reach Wisconsin voters before the final ballots are cast in the year’s _only_ statewide race before November. We can beat Elon Musk and show him that organized people are more powerful than billionaires. But we need your help. **Here’s your two-step checklist to defeating MAGA extremist Brad Schimel (and his new best friend Elon Musk) and electing Democrat Susan Crawford to protect the court’s liberal majority.**

**[Join the phone bank](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMbGj-ca0TYSsYMZBvIweYdJxZAP5xLg1YZaKIinIFmIx9h3smxOk-zlYSU8yWIxGtjZmiGsLAbHQReQW8mUQV5_sxZZuWnaJ9CAc_Y-fJAy2Iw7txeCyDjdwXJCfIzVJ8nxmemzesou1D3ZI-HpbkHk1neLtkGSQ6JHoNXJr4BJkMK8pLLr0Gf7FhSucVM4rH8s0lcZtsOo-wXr2CUSihh6C-M1iJ8GyEjTWpFNvi6mAjO-uqQzmDOzYMKSdPqiWY89viy0SNZkQ_lti6uU-1W8/4f9/gHuITqF-RvqUSz2zVVoQNA/h3/h001.f64lLPg9iUQDdbVe_1ZE9ir2QVyvxB1xa7CMk4GoSK4)** If you care about protecting access to safe abortions — we need your help in this race. I'm at Camden Yards to watch the Orioles play their first home game of the season. After a long winter, I’m ready to soak in the sun and cheer on our favorite team. Part of the reason I love Opening Day is because baseball is all about community. At Camden Yards, you can feel the energy in the crowd. It’s in the crack of the bat, the cheers from Eutaw Street, and the shared pride of a city that shows up for its own. The Orioles had a fantastic season last year, and whether you’re watching the game from your couch or joining me in the stands, I’m excited to cheer on the O’s alongside you. _**My prediction: This year the O’s are going to the World Series. Reply to this email to let me know what predictions you have this season.**_ Let’s go O’s! ⚾ Elevate, Wes

# Dan Bongino EXPLODES at Democrat for making every freaking thing about race
**By Richie McGinniss**
At the peak of the BLM madness, then-podcast host and former Secret Service agent Dan Bongino **[faced off with Democrat Congressman Hakeem Jeffries](https://substack.com/redirect/54977035-7fa3-40aa-8f83-39413700d16d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during a hearing on police justice reform.
[Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/54977035-7fa3-40aa-8f83-39413700d16d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Jeffries is now the minority leader for the House Democrats--the de-facto leader of the party--and Dan Bongino is now the Deputy Director of the FBI.
The June 10, 2020 clash encapsulates many of the reasons that the Democrats lost in 2024, with Jeffries' race-based worldview on full display, "Patrick Crusius [a mass shooter who killed 23 people in a War-Mart parking lot in 2019] was white is that correct?"
Bongino responded, "sir, I have no idea, I don't know his parentage."
Jeffries snapped back with the phrase that was uttered by every Democrat during that time, "Because Black Lives Matter, sir."
Bongino responded, "All lives matter, sir. Every single life matters."
In this singular back and forth, on display was the radicalized and racialized approach that the Democrat party took during that time. It is no coincidence that Trump made inroads into the Democrats black voting base in 2024, many have had it with America focusing so much on race, they just want the opportunity to put food on the table for themselves and for their families.

body:
Hi Peter,
I wanted to take a moment to say THANK YOU for all you’ve done to support my campaign since our launch. I know we’ve sent you a lot of emails over the past week, but there’s a reason for that.
This campaign isn’t backed by billionaires or big special interests, it’s powered by people chipping in a few dollars at a time because they believe in our campaign and believe that western Wisconsin deserves better. This is also the last time we’ll have the chance to show our strength this quarter.

From: Stacey Abrams, Fair Fight
Subject: Not duped. Not distracted. Not silenced.
I wasn’t expecting to hear Donald Trump attack me in front of a joint session of Congress earlier this month, but I can’t say I was surprised.
He’s obsessed with using the power of his platform to smear and attempt to silence those who challenge him. And he’s desperate to deflect attention from his broken promises. So he went after me, not because I did something wrong, but because I did something right.
It’s because I’ve fought alongside you and the Fair Fight team to protect the freedom to vote, a fundamental American value he tries to rip away. And it’s because — through the work he singled out — I’ve helped bring down costs for families, a promise he’s failed to keep.
To get away with his actual, unpopular agenda — taking money from working people to fund tax breaks for the ultra-rich — this petty tyrant and his complicit flunkies hope that Americans can be played for suckers, or lose focus.
And, chillingly, the authoritarian far right hopes they can undermine the ultimate failsafe in our democracy: the ability of the people to change the direction of our government at the ballot box.
But we will not be duped. We will not be distracted. And we will not be silenced.

---
Peter, Tonight is the deadline to reach our end-of-quarter fundraising goal, an important test for our movement to protect our nation and hard-working Americans from Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and their MAGA cronies. Within the first two months of Donald Trump’s presidency, he has shown that the only people he serves are his wealthy donors and allies — not the American people. Whether it’s coming after Medicaid and Social Security, firing federal workers, or waging a war on the Department of Education, Trump and Musk have made it clear that giving tax breaks to billionaires is their number one priority. I will continue doing everything I can to speak out against policies that only make your life harder. That means demanding answers from Trump’s cabinet of unqualified loyalists and calling out every attempt to scam the American people. But my voice alone isn’t enough. From: Eric H. Holder, Jr.
Date: Fri, Mar 28, 2025
Subject: 60 years from Bloody Sunday, our march is not yet finished
> Peter,
> This month, as we mark 60 years since Bloody Sunday, we're reminded that, as Dr. King said, the arc of the moral universe is long — but it bends towards justice.
> **What we need to understand is that the arc doesn't bend on its own.**
> It’s the dedication of all those brave men and women, seemingly ordinary but all extraordinary — who throughout history have risked, and too often given, their lives in order that others might live free.
> In the first days of March 1965, hundreds of peaceful activists, protesting to secure the right to vote, set out from Selma along the road to Montgomery. They made it as far as the foot of the Edmund Pettus Bridge before they were met with terrible violence at the hands of state and local law enforcement.
> **The events of this day not only steeled the resolve of America’s civil rights leaders — it compelled our national policymakers to take action.**
> With the passage of the landmark Voting Rights Act of 1965, our country finally created a robust safeguard for preventing discrimination and disenfranchisement in our elections. We finally had strong tools in place to deliver on the promise of fair representation for all voters, with fair district lines that would give communities the opportunity to elect the candidates of their choice.
> But ever since the Voting Rights Act was enacted, anti-democracy forces have sought to weaken it — in a continued, concerted effort to achieve unearned, illegitimate power at the expense of people of color.
> **60 years from Bloody Sunday, our march is not yet finished.** The U.S. Supreme Court is now set to rule in a Louisiana redistricting case that could overturn a key portion of that landmark law.
> While we likely won't know how the justices rule until June, we cannot stop working to protect our democracy and fight for fair maps. We cannot afford to give in to cynicism and doubt. We cannot be fatigued, overwhelmed, or indifferent.
> Our heroes of the civil rights movement showed us what courage looks like in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds. We must honor their legacy by continuing their unfinished work with the same determination and hope.
> In this moment of maximum danger to our country, it is now time for all those who love America most dearly to stand up and speak out for the principles that, at our best, define the nation. We have a sacred charge to uphold the legacy of those who gave their lives so that we may all have the right to vote.
> **It’s why All On The Line is leading the march towards a higher ideal — an ideal where every voter is empowered, transparency is non-negotiable, and electoral maps accurately reflect the will of the people.**
> Together, we hold leaders accountable, tirelessly advocate for fair maps across the nation, and unwaveringly uphold the core principles of democracy reform and election integrity.
> With your support, we’re preparing to stop potential efforts by partisan actors to steal more congressional seats through extreme gerrymandering. We’re working to ensure an accurate count in the next census that leads to fair maps for the next decade. And we’re standing alongside voters as they demand the fair representation that is their birthright.
> [**I’m grateful that you’ve helped make this ongoing work possible, and I hope you’ll help continue fighting for our democracy alongside All On The Line.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/104899255/536809190/-766669867?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_AGEOQ2_email_20250331-AOTL-Tier1-AGEOQ2-EHH_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250331-AOTL-Tier1-AGEOQ2-EHH_&utm_campaign=AGEOQ2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjYyYWU3MTgyLTdiMGUtZjAxMS05MGNkLTAwMjI0ODJhOWZiNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=GXQ7UbgrtdPa7luXhL_YHbrfYpspdEFxUQCiY-c96s0=)

subject: March Madness and Roadshows
body:
Senator Anderson Legislative Newsletter
---
| | | [](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fcontent.govdelivery.com%2Faccounts%2FORLEG%2Fbulletins%2F3d77eec/1/01010195ee439944-da7b762b-4eba-4365-9e3b-b151ee38c43b-000000/wkfrJhzVCFUlhfl-NpVuvEqKeRHL6O8GXdNm1BkBMik=398 "View Online")
---|---
---
|
* * *
---
Welcome back to another newsletter! Things in Salem are gearing up with the first big deadline behind us- this means if a bill did not have a scheduled hearing and work session in a committee it is considered dead and will no longer be in consideration to make it to the Governor’s desk for a signature at the end of June.
One bill that made its way through this process already is HCR 16. This resolution honors a son of Philomath, Oregon, Specialist Four Paul Jeffrey “Jeff” Cochran, who’s life and sacrifice embody the courage and selflessness we strive to uphold in Oregon. In 1966, Jeff enlisted in the Army, earning his Jump Wings with the 101st Airborne and deploying to Vietnam in 1967. On May 1, 1968, he gave his life in Thua Thien Province, leaving behind a legacy marked by the Bronze Star, Purple Heart, and Combat Infantryman Badge.
HCR 16 A not only commemorates Jeff’s sacrifices but celebrates a community’s resolve to remember. In 2019, his mother Beverly’s final wish gifted the family home to the city of Philomath- sparking the creation of the Paul J. Cochran Memorial Park. Dedicated last November, this park- built with a state grant and opened by his sister Shane- stands as a place to reflect on the human cost of war, right in the heart of my district. I see this as a testament to what we can achieve when we honor our past and invest in our future.
Speaking of balancing budgets, the Joint Ways and Means Committee their community budget hearings a few weeks ago. We kicked off the five meetings around the state in Gresham at Mt. Hood Community College to a large turnout. The second community hearing was in Astoria to a great turnout as well. Thank you to everyone who has shown up in person to get their requests heard.
Oregon operates on a two-year (biennial) budget cycle, beginning July 1 of odd-numbered years. The process starts with state agencies submitting their budget requests to the governor, who then crafts a recommended budget reflecting the Governor’s priorities. This proposal then goes to the Oregon Legislature, where the Joint Ways and Means Committee refines it through hearings, public input, and economic forecasts. The final budget, balancing revenue (like taxes and lottery funds) and expenditures (on education, health, etc.), must be approved by June’s end. Oregon, unlike the federal government, can’t deficit spend, ensuring a balanced budget every biennium.
In December, Governor Kotek released her recommended budget for the 2025-2027 biennium, proposing a total of $137.7 Billion in spending from all funds. This represents a 10.5% increase over the enacted budget for the 2023-2025 biennium. Key components include:
* **General Fund Spending:** $37.4 billion, a 13.8% increase from the previous biennium. This is the largest discretionary pool, primarily fueled by personal and corporate income taxes, which accounted for about 75% of tax revenue in 2015 (a trend that has largely continued).
* **Lottery Funds:** $1.9 billion, up 12.2% from the previous biennium.
* **Federal Funds:** $36.8, an 8.5% increase from the previous biennium. A significant portion of the total budget- this supports programs like Medicaid, education and housing. This will be interesting to watch.
* **Other Funds:** These include fees, licenses and specific taxes (e.g., gas taxes for transportation), often dedicated to purposes like human services or the Public Employee Retirement System (PERS).

Governor Kotek’s budget sounds noble- housing, schools and mental health, all important things. However, this is a 17% jump from the current biennium, and that’s reckless when we’re staring down a potential 9.7-billion-dollar hole if Trump’s federal cuts hit hard. Over 30% of our state budget relies on federal funds, and with a 1.3 trillion-dollar national deficit, we can’t assume that cash will keep flowing.
With the Federal government eyeing cuts many scenarios have been discussed to adjust for federal uncertainty. The final budget is due in June which hinges on May’s revenue forecast and federal policy clarity. In short, Oregon’s proposed General Fund budget aims to build on past gains- housing, health and schools- while bracing for a federal cut that could force tough choices.
Looking ahead to the 2025-2027 biennium (July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027) the latest revenue forecast indicates 37.8 billion in general fund resources. Only the General Fund and Lottery Funds are directly controlled by the legislature for flexibility allocation. The rest is restricted by federal rules or state regulations. The framework as of now is:
* Allocates 11.4 billion to schools, matching Kotek’s figure.
* Boosts human services by nearly $2 billion dollars.
* Sets aside $100 million for emergencies (up from $50 million) and $590 million for reserves.
* Targets $271.9 million in reductions, avoiding ongoing costs.

Just days before the Joint Ways and Means Community hearings kicked off across the state the committee released their budget framework for the 2025-2027 biennium. This framework continues the current service levels for existing programs, including 11.4 billion into the State School Fund for K-12 education. This adds an additional half a billion dollars to what schools in the state are already funded. Oregon ranks at or near the bottom of all states in each category including 51st overall and 35th in return on investment for education spending. Oregon’s student National Association of Education Progress scores rank 42nd in the nation. Oregon also spends above average per pupil annually. All these figures show that putting more money into our education system is not working. More spending is not the answer. Oregon needs to reinstate graduation requirements, require all students take the standardized tests (including Public, Charter, and Private schools) and minimize the expenditures focused on non-academic services and initiatives.
As we move towards June’s final budget deadline, Oregon stands at a crossroads. Honoring heroes like Jeff Cochran reminds us of the grit and sacrifices that built this state- a legacy we protect not just with memorials, but with smart choices today. The Joint Ways and Means Committee’s $38 billion framework is a step towards fiscal sanity, holding the line on current services while building reserves for the stormy days federal cuts might bring. More spending isn’t the fix; it’s time to rethink how we deliver, from classroom to care, to put Oregonians’ dollars where they’ll work the hardest.
The 1.8 billion kicker shows we have revenue to spare. Let’s ease the tax burden and fuel growth, not government. These community hearings are your chance to weigh in, so join us at the next stop and help shape a budget that respects our past and secures our future. Together, we can keep Oregon strong, not just for the biennium, but for generations to come.
There are four more community hearings over the next month. If you are able to make it in person or virtually.

* * *

* * *
---
My wife and I attended the Pearls of Wisdom fundraising event at Oregon Coast Community College in Newport. Pearls of Wisdom benefits the OCCC Foundation which funds student scholarships and college programs.
* * *
---
I testified before the Senate Committee on Housing and Development on behalf of Senate Bill 6. This bill sets a 45-day limit for building departments to process and approve housing applications, effectively streamlining the building permit process for single and middle housing homes.
You can watch my full testimony [here.](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv=ZhxynYomlX4/1/01010195ee439944-da7b762b-4eba-4365-9e3b-b151ee38c43b-000000/4x-_gvQIJhtdbxApiwirZd0Njih-n-WRtooCAdmZChI=398)
A work session for this bill has been scheduled for April 7th.
* * *
---
I had the pleasure of meeting with Douglas County Justice of the Peace Machelle Briggs-Mayfield in my office last week.
* * *
---
I testified on Senate Bill 974 before the Senate Housing and Development Committee. SB 974 cuts the process time for land use applications in the Urban Growth Boundary by 50% by eliminating housing delays due to local design review and reimbursing legal and engineering fees to approved applicants.
You can watch my full testimony [here. ](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv=ZAJTuuNAnCY%26feature=youtu.be/1/01010195ee439944-da7b762b-4eba-4365-9e3b-b151ee38c43b-000000/v_7hxvLglx46jTB8JL4mLgvdMXMvEUMRxl3rKgGSJtc=398)
A work session is scheduled for the bill on April 7th.
* * *
---
Oregon Coast Community College stopped by to tell me about their Small Business Development Center.
* * *
---
My Legislative Director Michael and I met with Sammy's Place Oregon COAAST Network. Sammy's Place was formed to advocate for the needs of the I/DD Community and to provide a support for individuals and families within the community and to provide encouragement and skills they need to be self-advocates and to contribute meaningfully within their towns and counties.
* * *
---
We had our first Joint Ways and Means Community Hearing in Gresham at Mt. Hood Community College. What a great turn out! Thank you to everyone who attended in person and virtually.
* * *
---
Alexsander Arredondo Diaz a 9th grade student from McKay High School was a Senate Honorary Page for Senate Girod this last week. He sat with me on the floor during session and stopped by my office to learn a little bit more about Senate District 5.
* * *
---
I testified before the Senate Committee on Senate Bill 1062. This bill will require a study of local authority over regulated utility rates and works.
* * *
---
I had the honor of Carrying HRC 16 when this bill was heard and passed on the Senate Floor. Jeff Cochran gave his life in Thua Thien Provience during the Vietnam war. HCR 16 A not only commemorated Jeff's sacrifices but celebrates a community's resolve to remember. Thank you to Jeff's sister Shane who joined me on the floor during the vote.
* * *
---
I sat down with my Co-host Bryan Iverson of Crosstabs and Port of Coos Commissioner Arnie Roblan to discuss a key project for the Port of Coos and the Pacific Coast Intermodal Port- which will be the first fully ship-to-rail facility on the U.S. West Coast.
Listen to the full podcast episode [here.](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Frightnoworegon.com%2F2025%2F03%2F30%2Flisten-crosstabs-podcast-former-co-speaker-arnie-roblan-and-senator-dick-anderson%2F/1/01010195ee439944-da7b762b-4eba-4365-9e3b-b151ee38c43b-000000/cmG3Kucrvf1z9xFxGwUiu59ZjN4S-WEc-c290zLc-m8=398)
* * *
---
The Rhododendron Festival Court stopped by the Capitol to meet with elected officials in the district. Be sure to check out Rhody Days if you are in the Florence area in May!
* * *
---
I got to spend some time with a few more honorary pages. James Tolan is an 8th grader at Taft 7-12 in Lincoln City, and Ryder Nash who is Senator Nash's grandson. Thank you both for spending part of your Spring Break at the Capitol!
* * *
---
We had our Joint Ways and Means Committee meeting in Astoria. There was a great turnout! Here is former Senator Betsy Johnson (Far Left) testifying for a Capital Construction Request.
* * *
---
* * *
---
[SB 5](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Folis.oregonlegislature.gov%2Fliz%2F2025R1%2FMeasures%2FOverview%2FSB5/1/01010195ee439944-da7b762b-4eba-4365-9e3b-b151ee38c43b-000000/s4BKVkY-D5WyFT4mXpzhAfgS-z8TYNBJJ2FTyJHhQno=398)\- Requires the governing board of each public university in this state to adopt a personnel policy that includes institutional standards for faculty qualifications. Things in Salem are gearing up with the first big deadline behind us- this means if a bill did not have a scheduled hearing and work session in a committee it is considered dead and will no longer be in consideration to make it to the Governor’s desk for a signature at the end of June. One bill that made its way through this process already is HCR 16. This resolution honors a son of Philomath, Oregon, Specialist Four Paul Jeffrey “Jeff” Cochran, who’s life and sacrifice embody the courage and selflessness we strive to uphold in Oregon. In 1966, Jeff enlisted in the Army, earning his Jump Wings with the 101st Airborne and deploying to Vietnam in 1967. On May 1, 1968, he gave his life in Thua Thien Province, leaving behind a legacy marked by the Bronze Star, Purple Heart, and Combat Infantryman Badge. HCR 16 A not only commemorates Jeff’s sacrifices but celebrates a community’s resolve to remember. In 2019, his mother Beverly’s final wish gifted the family home to the city of Philomath- sparking the creation of the Paul J. Cochran Memorial Park. Dedicated last November, this park- built with a state grant and opened by his sister Shane- stands as a place to reflect on the human cost of war, right in the heart of my district. I see this as a testament to what we can achieve when we honor our past and invest in our future. Speaking of balancing budgets, the Joint Ways and Means Committee their community budget hearings a few weeks ago. We kicked off the five meetings around the state in Gresham at Mt. Hood Community College to a large turnout. The second community hearing was in Astoria to a great turnout as well. Thank you to everyone who has shown up in person to get their requests heard. Oregon operates on a two-year (biennial) budget cycle, beginning July 1 of odd-numbered years. The process starts with state agencies submitting their budget requests to the governor, who then crafts a recommended budget reflecting the Governor’s priorities. This proposal then goes to the Oregon Legislature, where the Joint Ways and Means Committee refines it through hearings, public input, and economic forecasts. The final budget, balancing revenue (like taxes and lottery funds) and expenditures (on education, health, etc.), must be approved by June’s end. Oregon, unlike the federal government, can’t deficit spend, ensuring a balanced budget every biennium. In December, Governor Kotek released her recommended budget for the 2025-2027 biennium, proposing a total of $137.7 Billion in spending from all funds. This represents a 10.5% increase over the enacted budget for the 2023-2025 biennium. Key components include: General Fund Spending: $37.4 billion, a 13.8% increase from the previous biennium. This is the largest discretionary pool, primarily fueled by personal and corporate income taxes, which accounted for about 75% of tax revenue in 2015 (a trend that has largely continued). Lottery Funds: $1.9 billion, up 12.2% from the previous biennium. Federal Funds: $36.8, an 8.5% increase from the previous biennium. A significant portion of the total budget- this supports programs like Medicaid, education and housing. This will be interesting to watch. Other Funds: These include fees, licenses and specific taxes (e.g., gas taxes for transportation), often dedicated to purposes like human services or the Public Employee Retirement System (PERS). Governor Kotek’s budget sounds noble- housing, schools and mental health, all important things. However, this is a 17% jump from the current biennium, and that’s reckless when we’re staring down a potential 9.7-billion-dollar hole if Trump’s federal cuts hit hard. Over 30% of our state budget relies on federal funds, and with a 1.3 trillion-dollar national deficit, we can’t assume that cash will keep flowing. With the Federal government eyeing cuts many scenarios have been discussed to adjust for federal uncertainty. The final budget is due in June which hinges on May’s revenue forecast and federal policy clarity. In short, Oregon’s proposed General Fund budget aims to build on past gains- housing, health and schools- while bracing for a federal cut that could force tough choices. Looking ahead to the 2025-2027 biennium (July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027) the latest revenue forecast indicates 37.8 billion in general fund resources. Only the General Fund and Lottery Funds are directly controlled by the legislature for flexibility allocation. The rest is restricted by federal rules or state regulations. The framework as of now is: Allocates 11.4 billion to schools, matching Kotek’s figure. Boosts human services by nearly $2 billion dollars. Sets aside $100 million for emergencies (up from $50 million) and $590 million for reserves. Targets $271.9 million in reductions, avoiding ongoing costs. Just days before the Joint Ways and Means Community hearings kicked off across the state the committee released their budget framework for the 2025-2027 biennium. This framework continues the current service levels for existing programs, including 11.4 billion into the State School Fund for K-12 education. This adds an additional half a billion dollars to what schools in the state are already funded. Oregon ranks at or near the bottom of all states in each category including 51st overall and 35th in return on investment for education spending. Oregon’s student National Association of Education Progress scores rank 42nd in the nation. Oregon also spends above average per pupil annually. All these figures show that putting more money into our education system is not working. More spending is not the answer. Oregon needs to reinstate graduation requirements, require all students take the standardized tests (including Public, Charter, and Private schools) and minimize the expenditures focused on non-academic services and initiatives. As we move towards June’s final budget deadline, Oregon stands at a crossroads. Honoring heroes like Jeff Cochran reminds us of the grit and sacrifices that built this state- a legacy we protect not just with memorials, but with smart choices today. The Joint Ways and Means Committee’s $38 billion framework is a step towards fiscal sanity, holding the line on current services while building reserves for the stormy days federal cuts might bring. More spending isn’t the fix; it’s time to rethink how we deliver, from classroom to care, to put Oregonians’ dollars where they’ll work the hardest. The 1.8 billion kicker shows we have revenue to spare. Let’s ease the tax burden and fuel growth, not government. These community hearings are your chance to weigh in, so join us at the next stop and help shape a budget that respects our past and secures our future. Together, we can keep Oregon strong, not just for the biennium, but for generations to come. There are four more community hearings over the next month. If you are able to make it in person or virtually. name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: Barbarism.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
We have to fight for each other.
#
If we do not assert ourselves and enshrine our rights — and demand healthcare, and education, and dignity — the alternative is barbarism, which is what we are contending with now.
The fact that people are choosing between medicine and rent is barbarism.
The fact that people are worried about whether they will be on the streets every 4 weeks is barbarism.
The fact that every time a person has an ache or a pain, and they’re scared that it could either be a sore joint or cancer, but they can’t find out because they can’t afford the doctor? **This is barbarism.**
If we do not demand — and not only demand, but win — unions, healthcare, wages, and ending endless war, then we will condemn ourselves to barbarism.
I refuse to give up. I refuse to submit myself to that future. That’s not a life.
And so to live, **we have to fight for each other**. We have to stand with each other. We have to fight for this vision and this world.
[If you can, will you make a $5 contribution – or any amount that is meaningful to you – to help power our fight for transformative change? name: Sarah McBride
subject: Trans Day of Visibility
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Today is Trans Day of Visibility, a day to celebrate the growing representation of transgender people in business, the arts, and politics.
#
Today is Trans Day of Visibility, a day to celebrate the growing representation of transgender people in business, the arts, and politics. And when it comes to trans representation, it’s safe to say that we’ve come a _long way_ since I was a kid.
But this year’s Trans Day of Visibility hits differently than in years past. This is a frightening time for so many in our country.
But we must remain firm in our values and our vision in this moment — and, just as importantly, we should never give up on our ability to win over more people to more fully see our humanity and support our rights. It’s not always fair work, and it’s certainly not always easy work, but through the power of our proximity we can still open the hearts and change the minds of imperfect or unlikely allies.
That’s what we celebrate on this Trans Day of Visibility. Our visibility not only has the ability to inspire one another. It also has the capacity to push past the caricatures to invite more people in, to grow the tent of allies, to defeat the hateful attacks, and to lay the foundation for freedom and safety for trans people in every corner of our country and every part of our globe.
Growing up, I never imagined that I would one day serve in public office — let alone Congress — as my authentic self. But last November, because of hundreds of thousands of voters and supporters in Delaware and across the country, **we shattered the national lavender glass ceiling and proved that our democracy can be big enough for all of us.**
And as the first trans member of Congress to be elected, the way I can _guarantee_ I’m not the last is to quite simply be the best member of Congress that I can be. To continue to fight for what’s right and for who needs it most. And to show that trans people are multi-dimensional human beings.
That’s exactly what I plan to do — and I’m going to need your help every step of the way.
**Because in addition to Trans Day of Visibility, today is also important for another reason. We’re coming up on a critical end-of-quarter fundraising deadline at midnight tonight, after which we’ll have to publicly report all of our fundraising so far this year.**
[**So if you can, will you pitch in $5 to my campaign before midnight and help us reach our $110,000 goal for the first quarter?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20250331-1?refcode=em20250331-1865&amount=5&refcode2=1865_21716_JYj3iR&akid=1865%2E21716%2EJYj3iR)
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20250331-1?amount=5&refcode=em20250331-1865&refcode2=1865_21716_JYj3iR&akid=1865%2E21716%2EJYj3iR)**
In solidarity,
Sarah McBride

Tonight at midnight, we close the books on our first quarterly fundraising deadline since Donald Trump took office.
When it's over, we'll take stock of our resources and make some difficult decisions about where we can afford to make investments... and where we can't.
That's why we're asking you to donate today. $3. That's the ask.
$3 to help us expand strong gun laws in states where Democrats have the numbers to act.
$3 to help us fight back against Republican attempts to erode our gun laws in Congress or in states they have the numbers to act.
$3 to help us elect a Congress that will stand up to Donald Trump, Kash Patel, and those who prioritize the profits of gun manufacturers over the safety of our communities.
We know that $3 may not seem like it can do all of those things. But when so many people are chipping in what they can on the days they can, it adds up fast. So please:

Friend – the latest poll in **FL-6** has me locked in a dead heat with my radical leftist opponent **inside the******margin of error****.
We are staring down the barrel of a loss that could rip Congress apart and unleash chaos.
The other side smells blood in the water, and they’re pouring in **_millions of dollars_** to buy this race... And if the latest poll is any indication, **their strategy might be working**.

[DEFEND THE MAJORITY](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.com/click/e13055441/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUud2lucmVkLmNvbS9yYW5keS1maW5lLWZvci1jb25ncmVzcy9yZl9kb25fb21fZXJfcmYtbW9lX3JzXzIwMjUwMzMx/SZW1haWxfZnJlZXRoaW5rZXJkYWlseV9jb20yNTAzMzE/LbmNsWWx2dTNLZQ/qP3V0bV90ZXJtPWZ0ZDEmX25saWQ9YXBFSlhKejhVNiZfbmhpZHM9bmNXR1F1N0VBQ3oza0tscw/gZ-sgNw/s0m22adab1b)
